title: Briefing: India, France, Italy, South Africa, Serbia, Canada, Germany and Albania
script: Good morning. It's Wednesday, November fourth, and this is the Unowned briefing: the stories that matter, checked and graded. It's read by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our published timelines.
Every item carries our grade. Confirmed means independent outlets agree. Reported means one source so far. Disputed means the accounts conflict. And alleged is one side's claim.
Here are the top stories.
India. Today: Delhi counsel consents to criminal contempt case against Cockroach Janta Party legal head.
France. Today: CGT, FSU, FO and Solidaires file urgent court appeal as prefecture approves Saint‑Brieuc route.
Italy. Today: Rete degli Studenti Medi coordinator urges more school funding as students protest for teachers.
South Africa. Today: South African government says asylum seekers and refugees barred from voting by law.
Serbia. On Monday: Serbia prosecutor orders action on student complaints against criminal police chief Marko Kričak.
Canada. On Monday: Nine British Columbia First Nations file court applications to quash Pacific Link designation, Ottawa offers 10% stake.
Germany. On Monday: Education Minister Karin Prien deems youth protests legitimate, pled.
Albania. On Monday: Jailed Tirana mayor Erion Veliaj accuses Prime Minister Edi Rama of orchestrating his prison transfer.
Now the details.

India. Today: Delhi government counsel gave consent for criminal contempt proceedings against the Cockroach Janta Party's legal head over posts alleging a Saket court judge acted on outside orders, calling his view prima facie; the Delhi High Court will decide whether the case goes ahead, ETV Bharat reports. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, ETV Bharat, and isn't yet confirmed by a second. Coming up: The Special Executive Magistrate hearing for the CJP leaders summoned over the Jantar Mantar protest listed for the third week of November.

France. Today: The CGT, FSU, FO and Solidaires unions said they filed an urgent court appeal on the morning of November fourth over the Saint-Brieuc march route, which the prefecture then approved; Ouest-France reports the unions questioned the delay and ‘difficulties of dialogue’, saying they had declared the route on October nineteenth. We grade that reported: so far only Ouest-France has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation. Also today: The FSU teachers' union stated on Bluesky that the general secretary of the Italian trade union FLC CGIL expressed support for the November fifth mobilization and announced that Italian students and education personnel will mobilize on November twentieth to defend public education. That's their own claim, posted on their channel, and we grade it alleged. Coming up: Turnout and outcome of the unions' November fifth interprofessional strike and demonstration.

Italy. Today: The national coordinator of the Rete degli Studenti Medi school-student network tells la Repubblica that the government should invest more in schools, and that fewer staff would lower the quality of teaching. Students say they are protesting for teachers as well as for themselves. We grade that reported: so far only la Repubblica has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation. Coming up: Turnout and outcome of the CGIL general strike called for November twentieth.

South Africa. Today: The South African Government said on X, on local-election day, that asylum seekers and refugees may not vote. Its graphics cite the Refugee Regulations, which it says bar them from political activity, and the Electoral Act, which it says limits voting to registered citizens aged 18 or over. That's the authority's own claim, from its official statement, and we grade it alleged until independent reporting backs it up. Coming up: The new asylum appointment system Home Affairs said would be in place by November tenth.

Serbia. On Monday, November second: Serbia's Supreme Public Prosecutor's Office orders the Belgrade prosecutors to act on student complaints against criminal police chief Marko Kričak over an August 2025 incident in a Government of Serbia garage, which had gone more than a year without result, Vreme reports. The paper says Kričak, detained on November first, was still in custody on November third. We grade that reported: so far only Vreme has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation. Coming up: Formation of the new government and the choice of prime minister.

Canada. On Monday, November second: Nine British Columbia First Nations announce Federal Court applications to quash the Pacific Link national-interest designation, saying Ottawa did not adequately consult them. Ottawa says it consulted more than 110 Indigenous communities and will offer a minimum 10 per cent ownership stake, The Globe and Mail and the Vancouver Sun report; Cold Lake First Nation filed the first challenge in October. Our grade: confirmed by independent reporting. Coming up: Whether binding Pathways carbon-storage agreements are signed by the November fifteenth target.

Germany. On Monday, November second: Germany's Education Minister Karin Prien calls the concerns of the young people who marched in more than 30 cities on October thirty-first "legitimate and extremely relevant" and promises more dialogue, and SPD politicians call for a national education summit; these are proposals, not policy changes so far, The Local reports. We grade that reported: so far only The Local Germany has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation. Coming up: Gen Z regelt plans another countrywide protest on November fourteenth.

Albania. On Monday, November second: Albania's jailed Tirana mayor Erion Veliaj accuses Prime Minister Edi Rama of orchestrating his prison transfer, which the government denies. Veliaj, held in pre-trial detention on corruption charges he denies, also said Justice Minister Toni Gogu demanded he give up control of the city, Tirana Times reports; the claims, relayed in part by his lawyer, are unverified. Our grade: disputed. The sides tell it differently, and both versions are on the story page.
That's the Unowned briefing for Wednesday, November fourth. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com. Thanks for listening.
